title: JRFK backup reports empty USB SD reader as mounted, and reports SD card missing when inserted
resolution: Fixed in rfk_backup.sh: 1) Checked media size via lsblk to verify capacity > 0, correctly identifying empty card readers as unpopulated. 2) Replaced substring check on /proc/mounts with explicit detection of root and boot block devices using findmnt, preventing automounted desktop partitions from disqualifying valid USB SD targets. 3) Added unmount_target_partitions() to safely detach any desktop automounted target partitions before piclone or dd executes.
comments: Root Cause Analysis: 1) Empty USB SD reader creates /dev/sda block device with 0 bytes capacity, but script only checks [ -b /dev/sda ], erroneously reporting target_found=true with 0 bytes. 2) When an SD card is inserted, desktop udisks2/pcmanfm automounts partitions (/dev/sda1, /dev/sda2) to /media/pi/. The script check "! grep -qs $dev /proc/mounts" substring-matches the mounted partitions, causing find_target_dev() to discard the valid SD card and report target missing. Fix required: Check that media capacity > 0 (size > 0), and check that /dev/sda is not the active rootfs/boot device without rejecting automounted target partitions.
